text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) and ruling coalition agree to talk again about tax reform.
- Regional public broadcasters SDR and SWF to merge.
- Prosecutors looking into possibility of launching investigation into role of Iranian foreign minister in case of four dissidents killed in Berlin in 1992.
- Alexandre Lamfalussy, head of European Monetary Institute, calls for further consolidation in European budgets.
- Federal Labour Office head Bernhard Jagoda calls for more flexibilty and innovation in the jobs market.
HANDELSBLATT
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl and SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine continue game of tactics over tax reform.
- Dieter Schulte, head of German Trade Union Federation (DGB), distances himself from suggestion by leader of IG Metall trade union to cut working week to 32 hours.
- Iranian trade delegation calls off trip to Germany.
- Education Minister Juergen Ruettgers to present programme to improve situation in apprenticeship market.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Coalition and SPD say an agreement on tax policy is possible.
- Federal Labour Office paid out 5.97 billion marks in unemployment benefit in first three months of 1997, 800 million marks more than in the same period last year.
- Inflation rate slows in March.
- Liberal Free Democrats (FDP) say they will decide on Monday whether to approve plans for pension reforms.
DIE WELT
- DGB plans big day of protests against government policy on May 1.
- Ifo institute says recession in east German construction industry continues.
- Medium-sized businesses will continue to shed staff over next half year, survey says.
